memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The animals you choose must be year-old males without defect, and you may take
them from the sheep or the goats." - Ex 12:5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The lamb had to be without defect. Not the weak one, not the injured one, not
the animal the family could most easily spare. The best of the flock.

This mattered because the lamb was standing in the place of the firstborn son.
A substitute for a life must be worthy. God would not accept something damaged
in exchange for something precious.

Centuries later, Peter writes to Christians about their redemption: it came "not
with perishable things such as silver or gold... but with the precious blood of
Christ, a lamb without blemish or defect" (1 Pet 1:18-19). Peter is reaching
back to this exact verse. Every spotless Passover lamb for fifteen hundred years
was pointing to One who would be truly without defect, not merely physically but
morally. Jesus alone could say, "Which of you convicts me of sin?" (John 8:46).

That is why our salvation is secure. It does not rest on the quality of our
faith on a given morning. It rests on the quality of the Lamb. He was examined
by Pilate, by Herod, by His enemies, and no fault was found in Him.

We bring nothing spotless to God. Christ brought Himself.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you trusting in the quality of your faith or the quality of your Saviour?
2. What does it mean to you that Jesus was examined and found faultless?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord Jesus, You are the Lamb without blemish. I have nothing perfect to offer,
so I offer You. Thank You for standing in my place. Amen.
